To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) once the range of scores was equated, language and theory ofmind were related; (ii) there was no evidence that syntax played a unique role in relation to theory of mind; and (iii) working memory was not a mediating factor in the relation between languageand theory of mind, or a facilitator of later false belief.

(1) there is a bidirectional relation, but not a unidirectional relation, between language and theory mind; (2) syntax plays no unique role in the relation between language in theory of mind; (3) there is not one aspect of either syntax or semantics that is more predictive of later false belief; and (4) working memory plays no role in the relation of either language or false belief.

(1) the relation between language (syntax and semantics) and theory of mind is bidirectional, and (2) working memory is neither the cause nor the effect of the relation between language syntax/semantics and theory of mind
